blocks.text: In B1-15 you have learned to read the titles; You're gonna be in the articles now. Each section of a newspaper has its own small vocabulary, which repeats itself almost the same every day: in a bad weather news they always come back ⁧هُطُولُ أَمْطَارٍ غَزِيرَةٍ⁩ , ⁧فِرَقُ الإِنْقَاذِ⁩ and have not been injured, in economics ⁧مُعَدَّلُ التَّضَخُّمِ⁩ and ⁧عَجْزُ المِيزَانِيَّةِ⁩ . In this unit you learn the essential vocabulary of seven areas (politics, economy, society, accidents, weather, courts, sport), especially as placements: the verb or adjective that always accompanies a certain name. For the courts only the general lexicon of the chronicles is studied, on civil and administrative cases. All the news is invented. Two weeks.

blocks.text: Materials This unit, dictionary by root, a chronicle notebook (one sheet per section), voice synthesis scripts, session with the tutor; optional: a news site in Arabic
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize the sections of an Arabic newspaper and their typical vocabulary;
2. understanding and using the most frequent placements of politics, economy and society ( ⁧أَدْلَى بِصَوْتِهِ⁩ , ⁧مُعَدَّلُ التَّضَخُّمِ⁩ , ⁧نَظَّمَ⁩
⁧اعْتِصَامًا⁩ );
3. read short news of accidents and weather and their fixed formulas ( ⁧لَقِيَ مَصْرَعَهُ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ تُسَجَّلْ إِصَابَاتٌ⁩ );
4. understanding the general vocabulary of judicial reports ( ⁧جَلْسَة⁩ , ⁧غَرَامَة⁩ , ⁧اِسْتِئْنَاف⁩ ) and sports ( ⁧تَعَادَلَ⁩ , ⁧تَأَهَّلَ⁩ , ⁧هَزِيمَة⁩ );
5. organize the vocabulary for roots and for placements in a notebook of the chronicle.
